questions.question: Jade has 12 stickers. She gives 5 to her friend. How many stickers does Jade have now?
questions.explain: Taking away means you subtract. 12 take away 5 is 7. The trap is adding 12 and 5 together, which gives 17 — that would mean more stickers, not fewer.

questions.question: There are 15 apples in a basket. You take 3 to eat. How many apples are left?
questions.explain: Taking 3 apples away means 15 minus 3, which is 12. Don't add 15 and 3 to get 18 — eating apples means they go, not come.

questions.question: Tom has 8 toys. Lee has 13 toys. How many more toys does Lee have?
questions.explain: How many more means take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 13 take away 8 is 5. Saying 13 just names Lee's toys, and 21 is what you get if you add them up.

questions.question: Your jar has 14 marbles. Your friend's jar has 9. How many more marbles do you have?
questions.explain: How many more means take 9 away from 14, which is 5. Saying 14 just names your own jar, and 23 is what you get if you add both jars together.

questions.question: Mrs. Chen puts 16 cookies on a plate. The kids eat 7. How many cookies are still on the plate?
questions.explain: Eating cookies takes them away, so 16 take away 7 is 9. Adding 16 and 7 to get 23 would mean more cookies magically appeared on the plate.

questions.question: Maya stacks 11 blocks high. Her brother stacks 17 blocks high. How many blocks taller is his stack?
questions.explain: How many taller means take 11 away from 17, which is 6. Saying 17 just names his stack, and 28 is what you get if you add both stacks together.

questions.question: You have 13 lollipops. You eat 4. What do you do to find how many are left?
questions.explain: Eating lollipops takes them away, so you subtract 4 from 13. Putting them together or counting on would give you more lollipops, which is not what happened.

questions.question: Aya has 9 gummy bears. Kip has 15. To find how many more Kip has, what do you do?
questions.explain: How many more means take the smaller number away from the bigger one. Putting them together gives a total, not a difference.

questions.question: Grandpa has 15 tomatoes. He gives 6 away, then picks 3 more. How many does he have now?
questions.explain: First take 6 away from 15 to get 9. Then 3 more means you add 3 to get 12. The trick is to add when more come and subtract when some go.

questions.question: Sara has 14 crayons. That is 6 more than Ben. How many crayons does Ben have?
questions.explain: Sara has 6 more, so Ben has 6 fewer. Take 6 away from 14 to get 8. Adding 6 to get 20 would make Ben have more than Sara, which is not right.

questions.question: Lena's tower is 16 blocks. Max's tower is 11 blocks. A friend says, 'Lena's is 27 blocks taller.' What went wrong?
options: He just said the bigger one
He just said the smaller one
questions.explain: 27 is what you get if you add 16 and 11 together. To find how many taller, you take 11 away from 16 to get 5.

questions.question: Jake has 18 toy cars. He gives 5 to his brother, then 3 to his sister. How many does he have now?
questions.explain: You take 5 away, then take 3 more away. 18 minus 5 is 13, and 13 minus 3 is 10. Adding all the numbers to get 26 would mean more cars appeared out of nowhere.
